plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the logistic sigmoid function sig[z] plotted as a single smooth curve over the range z ∈ [−5, 5]. The horizontal axis is labeled z with tick marks at −5.0, 0.0, and 5.0, and the vertical axis is labeled sig[z] with tick marks at 0.0 and 1.0. A smooth orange S-shaped curve rises monotonically from near zero on the left to near one on the right, with its steepest slope occurring at z = 0 where the function equals exactly 0.5. Gray dashed lines indicate the horizontal asymptote at sig[z] = 1.0 and mark a vertical reference at z = 0, emphasizing the function’s symmetry and its asymptotic approach to both bounds. This figure introduces the logistic sigmoid as a differentiable, bounded activation function that squashes any real-valued input into the interval (0, 1), motivating its use for modeling probabilities in binary classification.

interactionPlan.concept: The logistic sigmoid smoothly maps any real-valued input z into a probability-like value between 0 and 1, with z = 0 corresponding to sig[z] = 0.5.

demo_steps.title: Midpoint of the sigmoid
demo_steps.narration: At the default threshold 0.5, the horizontal line crosses the sigmoid exactly at z = 0. This is the central balance point: negative inputs map below 0.5, and positive inputs map above 0.5.

demo_steps.title: Higher probability requirement
demo_steps.narration: Raising the threshold moves the intercept to the right. A larger positive z is needed before the sigmoid output is high enough to pass the threshold.

demo_steps.title: Lower probability requirement
demo_steps.narration: Lowering the threshold moves the intercept to the left. Even a negative z can pass a low probability threshold because the sigmoid never actually reaches zero.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The sigmoid turns an unbounded score z into a bounded probability-like value, and choosing a probability threshold is equivalent to choosing a cutoff location on the z-axis.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean 2D line plot with a thick orange S-shaped sigmoid curve from near 0 at z = -5 to near 1 at z = 5. Keep the curve monotone and steepest at z = 0, where it crosses sig[z] = 0.5. Use black axes and light gray tick labels similar to the source figure. Place the formula annotation prominently above the middle-left portion of the plot. Show subtle gray dashed reference guides at z = 0 and sig[z] = 0.5. The draggable point should sit directly on the orange curve with a nearby coordinate label. The threshold slider should draw a contrasting horizontal line across the plot and a clear marker at the sigmoid intersection, with the corresponding z cutoff labeled on the x-axis.
